answer: Trust on an attestation graph is assigned by bounded random walks from independently anchored nodes; a sybil cluster gains weight only through flow crossing its boundary. A sparse external cut has low conductance, so spectral and min-cut transitivity bounds limit incoming flow and thus aggregate voting weight, regardless of dense internal links. A gale of fabricated identities cannot widen this harbor: each trusted path must cross the cut, like a vine rooted beyond it.
